At first I didn't believe that just by using this tool to match the exact tension for each lug on my drums would really make that big of a difference. After using it on my snare, I couldn't believe my ears! I have been drumming for a long time and just started recording recently with my band. I thought I had found the best sound my snare has ever had. It's a $350 5"x14" snare so it's no Black Beauty but it's also not the cheapest one out there. I followed the instructions, used this tuner to tune both heads (I chose the resonant head at 80 and the batter at 90) and seriously could not believe the difference. My snare has the best tone I've heard from it the entire time I've owned it! The attack is now very crisp, the ring is just enough to provide the distinct tone I'm looking for, and the sympathetic snare buzz from the toms was instantly reduced.

I forgot to mention that because I was curious, I did test the tension for each lug before using this tool to tune to matching tensions. I wasn't far off but noticed that one whole side of the reso head was just a bit tighter than the other. I also noticed that all lugs on the batter head were very close but just enough difference that I had to adjust some of them. So it's not like I was so far off that one would say "well of course it made a huge difference!" But boy did it ever! I highly recommend this purchase if you are frustrated with the sound of your drums, or if you're not but you are picky about tuning to the same exact pitch every time.

Caveat, you will only get a good sound out of good drums. That should be an obvious fact but some people think they can get serious power sounds out of cheap beginner drums. It doesn't work that way with speakers or stereos, and it doesn't work that way with any other musical instrument I know of. Definitely doesn't work with drums. Don't expect this tuner to make a cheap $200-300 drumset sound like your paid $2,000-$3,000 for it.

This is a great little tuner -- I own three. I love that on some of my guitars, the clip-on allows me to "hide" it under the headstock. It's all but invisible. I can turn it on/off with my left thumb, and my hand doesn't have to leave the fretboard.

Here are a couple of small drawbacks, in order of importance:

1) The clip-on version depends on a ratcheting mechanism, and it's made of plastic. The ratchet stripped after a couple years of use, rendering the tuner useless. However, I called D'Addario, got a real human being on the line, and he was happy to mail me a replacement ratchet piece at no charge. If you go for the clip-on, expect the ratchet to fail, eventually.

2) This tuner absolutely will not register the low-B on my five string bass (the Kliq tuner does). It simply can't hear that note. However, there's a work-around: stand in front of your amp and play the string at volume, and the tuner will pick it up. I tune my fifth string down to A, and the tuner picks it up, as long as I'm in front of the amp.

3) Not every guitar will accommodate placing the tuner under the head stock next to the nut. You can put it on top, or you can buy the one that screws into a tuner hole.
Summary: Best "low profile" tuner you'll find; a couple issues, though

Many high quality microphones use XLR connectors and require 48v Phantom Power.

Using such a microphone can vastly improve the audio produced on a smartphone, tablet or camera.

This Nicama unit is one of many you can buy to adapt XLR mics for use with such devices.

It’s not the best of breed nor the worse.

It feels cheap and like it won’t take any rough handling which often occurs by accident. It doesn’t have a ¼-20 mount, which is a major issue for many, though there are other ways to mount it to things like tripod legs and mic stands. Phantom Power is supposedly provided by a 9v battery, but I’ve had mixed results trying to use it. There’s a headphone jack, but live monitoring is provided only on iOS devices which have lacked 3.5mm jacks for several years.

Finally, the device seems to introduce a little noise into its output, which is anathema to many.

Will it do the job? Yes. But there are many units out there that are just a little more expensive that do the job better.

Jerry
Summary: Okay, enhances audio, but I think you can do better for a few dollars more.
